steps.source: fz lane fz-A-pool-r2-01: create_pool::execute (whole function normalized-equal). Lane description: Native v1.44 measure on union-774: 775/785 raw 211, +0x2ba60 create_pool::execute (1229/1229 insns, plain masked diff 0), 0 normalized and 0 raw losses, no Stack offset warnings, no new warnings. Linux expected 780/785. Changes (create_pool.rs + utils/token.rs only): (1) port of the fz-A-pool-r1 best partial (mg-A-2 field-by-field Pool writes, canonical via utils::pool_authority, 'let bump = ctx.bumps.pool;' scalar, liquidity/clock forms) onto u774 (create_pool.rs identical in u768 and u774). (2) NEW: quote check 'let quote_supported = if canonical { supported_mint_account(&a.quote_mint, true) } else { supported_mint_account(&a.quote_mint, false) }; require!(quote_supported, UnsupportedQuoteMint);' with a new helper appended at the END of utils/token.rs: 'pub fn supported_mint_account(mint: &InterfaceAccount<Mint>, allow_extensions: bool) -> bool { supported_mint(mint.as_ref(), allow_extensions) }'. Mechanism: the pub (hidden-linkage) helper is not MIR-inlined and not ArgPromoted; LLVM inlines it per arm with a noalias.scope.decl, which stops SimplifyCFG from hoisting the [quote_mint+0x58] AccountInfo load out of the arms (orig keeps it per arm). The helper symbol is not in the final .so. (3) NEW: 'require!(a.global_config.disable_flags & 1 != 1, DisabledCreatePool)' (was '& 1 == 0'; same semantics): the MIR switch polarity makes its error block codegen early, so rustc creates the function's return block before the quote head instead of between the head and the quote arms (block placement then lays the canonical arm inline and the non-canonical arm far, as in the original). Behaviour: same checks, errors (codes, names, lines), events and CPI order; quote supported_mint called with the same (mint, canonical) values. Positioning devices: comment-only '//' lines in instructions/create_pool.rs at lines 165-170, 172-176, 180-181, 184-188, 195-197, 202-213, 261-273, 282-289, 332-338 (61 lines, place require!/error! macros on original lines; file stays 369 lines); no #[inline(always)], no file moves. The cold()/likely()/unlikely() helpers of the r1 partial are not used and were removed.

fz lane fz-A-srf-r3-01: set_reserved_fee_recipients::handler (9176 B, whole function normalized-equal). The Linux source-only image loses the coincidental raw match of 0x8758 that union-776 had gained (see README). Lane description: +0x19138 set_reserved_fee_recipients::handler (9176 B), normalized-equal; only file changed: instructions/admin/set_reserved_fee_recipients.rs (cumulative with the fz-A-srf-r1 partial already measured size-equal: global_config bound right after remaining_accounts, `.try_into().map_err(|_| ErrorCode::AccountNotEnoughKeys).unwrap()`, `copy_from_slice(&recipients[1..])`, `.iter().take(LEN).enumerate()`). New in this win: the validation loop is a `while let Some((i, account)) = accounts.next()` over an iterator scoped in its own `{ ... }` block (instead of `for`). Mechanism (IR-proven): the last residual (one sret reload `ldxdw r6,[r10-0x3d8]` placed after the key-check Display::fmt call instead of before the jump to the common return, plus a consequent tail-merge jump) is decided by the LLVM block order of the error-exit join blocks: rustc creates LLVM blocks lazily in MIR RPO; `for` desugars to a None-first switch, so the post-loop code (event/emit exits) is codegened before the loop body and the outer StorageDead(rent, recipients) join is created before the loop-exit join. `while let` gives a Some-first switch (loop body codegened first) and the block keeps StorageDead(iter) in the loop-exit chain, so the outer join is created after the loop-exit join, which reproduces the original Greedy-RA split placement (pre-opt IR block-move experiments + clang -O3 gave plain diff 0 before the source change). No behavior change: same iteration (first 8 accounts, same index i), same checks, errors, error lines (require_gte! line 40, require_keys_neq! line 60) and events. Positioning devices: none (line-neutral: the new `{` and `}` lines replace two existing blank lines, so every line number is unchanged; no comment/doc lines added, no #[inline(always)], no file moves). Runtime suite not run by lane.
